assets.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Production background asset for a premium Chinese Three Kingdoms duel card game, wide 16:9 landscape. A hand-painted ancient Chinese river pavilion seen from a seated player's perspective, broad charcoal lacquered wooden table occupies bottom 68 percent. River, distant misty mountains, military rooftops and a few sails through the pavilion occupy upper 32 percent. Thin dark wooden pillars at far left and right, a single subtle warm lantern at left edge, overcast afternoon. Low perspective, table extends to all bottom edges. Deliberately calm clean empty tabletop across center and lower middle for composited readable card game UI. Cohesive ink and opaque watercolor historical illustration, sophisticated desaturated blue-grey and muted dark brown, slight warm light on table, finely drawn physical details at distant edges only. Artwork itself, no interface. Absolutely NO cards, portraits, playing pieces, text, calligraphy, symbols, buttons, menus, borders, icons, logos, watermarks or dramatic lighting effects. No random weapons on foreground, no massive props blocking table. Quiet, legible, restrained, beautifully painted. 1920x1080 or larger wide landscape.
assets.editPrompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. This is the background asset of an interactive Chinese historical card game. Keep the exact painterly style, desaturated colors, soft light, pavilion, lantern and distant mountains/river. Change ONLY camera framing and table extent: the broad near-black charcoal lacquered wooden playing table must begin at exactly 28 percent of the image height and occupy ALL remaining bottom 72 percent down to the bottom edge. The horizon/river scene and railing must be entirely confined to the upper 28 percent. Tilt viewpoint slightly downward and move table away from the camera to accomplish this natural composition. The tabletop should have subtle fine wood grain, no bright gold reflections, few distracting plank seams. Side props stay at extreme upper edges; no objects in the middle or bottom of the table. No visible near edge of table, playing surface extends past frame. Upper 28 percent still provides lovely misty river landscape and pavilion context. Low contrast throughout the empty table so independent ivory UI cards at 40 percent height will clearly sit over wood, never river. Absolutely no cards, figures, UI, text, symbols, icons, logo, watermark. Same wide 16:9 image aspect ratio. This image must be ready as a clean complete background layer, not a screenshot mockup.

Use case: illustration-story. Production sprite atlas: exactly FIFTEEN equal square illustrations in a STRICT 5 COLUMN by 3 ROW edge-to-edge regular grid, landscape aspect ratio 5:3. Every tile exactly same size; perfectly aligned rows and columns, NO margins, gutters, borders or text. It will be sampled as a CSS sprite sheet. Each square is a separate original ink-and-watercolor illustration on warm ivory paper, Chinese Three Kingdoms historical card game art. Consistent art direction across all fifteen tiles: finely observed line drawing, dynamic yet restrained composition, muted charcoal ink, warm stone pigments, small cinnabar accents, tactile paper. NOT icons, actual miniature historical paintings. Keep subject in central 75% of each tile to allow inset crop.
READ ORDER left-to-right then top-to-bottom:
Row 1: (1) armored warrior forcefully thrusting a spear in battle, (2) nimble warrior sidestepping an incoming blade with swirling robe, (3) two ripe peaches on a peach branch still life, (4) abandoned timber bridge breaking across a river, (5) stealthy traveller leading a sheep along a riverbank.
Row 2: (1) scholar opening a scroll with an ingenious plan emerging as fine ink imagery, (2) two swordsmen facing each other in a duel, (3) strategist lending a sword to an armored soldier, (4) three cups of wine under blossoming peach trees, (5) a distant southern army advancing with banners through mist.
Row 3: (1) a volley of arrows crossing the sky above a battlefield, (2) baskets of ripe millet and golden grain with a village granary, (3) soldier's blade cleanly parrying a hostile strike, (4) courtly banquet in a distant pavilion with wine and musical instruments, (5) branching lightning striking an isolated old tower in a storm.
No Chinese characters, no letters, no rank or suit symbols, no labels, no card frames, no watermark. Each tile has pale paper edges so it fits into an independently composited parchment card. Beautiful serious historical illustration, no cartoon, no chibi, no 3D. EXACT 5 columns and 3 rows.

Use case: illustration-story. Production sprite atlas, EXACTLY SIXTEEN equal square historical paintings in a strict FOUR COLUMN by FOUR ROW edge-to-edge grid, square total image. Each tile same size and perfectly aligned, no outer margin, no gutters, no words or borders. Single consistent Chinese ink and muted watercolor on warm ivory paper, hand-painted Three Kingdoms card-game equipment illustrations, elegant real physical objects, finely drawn, no glowing fantasy magic. Center each complete subject in middle 75% of its tile. Each tile needs its own pale paper background.
Left to right, top to bottom, exact grid:
Row 1: ancient Chinese repeating crossbow with wooden magazine; a slim straight blue steel Chinese sword; a matched pair of straight Chinese swords crossing; a long polearm with a large green crescent blade.
Row 2: long dark serpentine spear; heavy battle axe with dark wooden haft; Chinese halberd with central spear point and two symmetrical crescent blades; elegant recurved bow and quiver.
Row 3: octagonal ancient bronze mirror with subtle eight trigram markings; a dark iron shield with stern guardian face embossing; red chestnut warhorse galloping; sandy brown sturdy travelling horse.
Row 4: dark purple-brown warhorse; white horse leaping a stream; black horse in a misty field; golden yellow horse with white hooves trotting.
Keep all weapons fully inside each tile, diagonal if needed, no bleed between cells. Illustration fills each tile but modest breathing room. No humans. Absolutely no text, labels, Chinese characters, suit/rank symbols, logos or watermark. Cohesive premium traditional card illustration, not icon graphics, not 3D render. EXACT 4 by 4 grid.

Use case: illustration-story. One production portrait atlas consisting of exactly TWO equal vertical portraits side by side, perfectly divided at 50% width, no gutter or frame. Total image ratio 4:3, each portrait 2:3. Original Chinese historical game character illustrations, sophisticated opaque watercolor and fine ink brushwork, detailed grounded faces and clothing, restrained dark blue-grey and brown, subtle warm light, misty grey river pavilion background. LEFT HALF: anonymous adult Chinese male military commander, early thirties, tied long black hair, short neat mustache, dark layered lamellar armor and muted red cloth at shoulder, chest-up three-quarter portrait facing slightly right, calm and focused. RIGHT HALF: anonymous adult Chinese female military commander, early thirties, tied black hair, practical dark lamellar armor and muted blue cloth, chest-up three-quarter portrait facing slightly left, calm and focused. No helmet covering faces. Both entirely clothed, believable anatomy, similar visual weight and crop. Do not depict famous identifiable Three Kingdoms characters or any official game character. Neither is a playable named hero; these are seat avatars. Faces must read at 90px wide. Elegant serious painterly art, no anime, no photorealism, no plastic CGI, no glamour, no extra objects, no text, no calligraphy, no rank symbols, no logos, no border.
